question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3: Was not'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 3,** "was not"** is the correct answer. 
 
• This is because **"Dinner"** is treated as a** singular** subject and requires the singular form of the verb "be" (i.e., "was") fo**r past events.** 
 
• The **"not" **is added to negate the sentence, indicating that the dinner was not a pleasant experience.

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: *'Dinner in the Great Hall that night **was not **a pleasant experience for Sunny. The (2) _____ about his shouting match with Umbridge had (3) _______ exceptionally fast even (4) ________ standards. He heard whispers all (5) ________ as he sat eating between Rob and Ravi.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1,** "were not"** is** incorrect because the subject** "Dinner" is singular – hence it needs the singular verb "was," not "were."
 
• Option 2, **"was neither"** is incorrect** because the neither/nor construction** is used to indicate that two or more things are not true or do not happen. But in this sentence, there's only one event being negated, which is the pleasant experience of dinner, therefore the use of "neither" is unnecessary.
 
• Option 4,** "is not"** is incorrect due to** tense inconsistency**. The event clearly took place in the past as indicated by "that night," so the verb should be in the past tense, "was," not in the present tense, "is."
